transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Before we get into the details of 'Afterimage Corridor,' I want to make sure we run through the full sign-off process today. I need input from technical production, music rights, accessibility, and visitor services before I can approve the operating package for the east gallery. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a technical production concern. My electrician load test found that the gallery circuit allocated to 'Afterimage Corridor' supports exactly two LED projection units totaling no more than 300 watts. The current draft calls for four LED projection units, so we have a capacity issue. I'm still waiting on the signed load sheet from the building engineer before I enter the result in the production file, but I wanted to get this on the table now since it directly affects the installation plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a music rights concern to flag. I've confirmed with the publisher that only a 42-second excerpt of the composition 'Night Transit' is cleared for this installation, and it must play once per visitor cycle rather than as a continuous loop. The current draft calls for a continuous audio loop, so we have a rights compliance issue. I also haven't yet attached the email confirmation to the rights register, but I wanted to get this on the table now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have an accessibility concern to flag. My walk-through found that visitors must enter through the east doorway — not the north doorway called for in the current draft — and the route must maintain a clear width of exactly 1.5 meters. I'm also revising the accessibility map after the gallery's temporary plinths are moved, so that's still in progress.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a visitor services concern to flag. I've confirmed with the heritage centre's fire warden that the installation must use timed cycles admitting no more than 12 visitors, with each cycle lasting exactly 8 minutes. This replaces the open walk-in admission called for in the current draft. I'm still waiting for the warden's countersigned visitor-flow note, but I wanted to get this on the table now since it directly affects the operating package.
transcript.speaker: A5

transcript.text: Thank you all for flagging these concerns. Let me summarise what I'm hearing before I make any decision. Jonah, we have a circuit capacity issue: the gallery circuit supports only two LED projection units at up to 300 watts, but the draft calls for four. Leila, we have a rights compliance issue: only a 42-second excerpt of 'Night Transit' is cleared, to play once per visitor cycle, not as a continuous loop. Owen, the accessible entry must be through the east doorway — not the north doorway in the draft — with a clear route width of 1.5 meters. And Nia, the fire warden requires timed cycles of no more than 12 visitors, each lasting exactly 8 minutes, replacing open walk-in admission. I also note that several of you are still waiting on signed documents — Jonah needs the building engineer's load sheet, Leila needs to attach the publisher email to the rights register, Owen is revising the accessibility map, and Nia is waiting on the warden's countersigned visitor-flow note. Before I issue my approval, I need to confirm: can each of you get those outstanding documents finalised and entered into the production file today? I don't want to approve an operating package with open paperwork.
transcript.speaker: A1
